scope: Isolated WebSocket result-channel prototype and test-driver assertion-allocation control on original PLY-3; not production behavior or M2 acceptance
method: Reapply the previously recorded disposable alternate transport, instrument its server to record channel authentication and every 128th large reply without retaining payloads, and use the external driver whose failed-response assertion formats its message only on failure. No forced garbage collection or resource-limit change.
channelEvidence: The socket authenticated, and its counter reached at least 1792 large replies. The complete 475563378-byte artifact stream and file hashes matched, so this run establishes use of the experimental path for a substantial part of the download, not necessarily every reply.
result: GUI Split, Extract, undo, complete download and GUI reopen completed. The first post-reopen public-MCP geometry digest timed out; subsequent geometry and undo/redo checks were not reached. Job peak was 4353630208 bytes, exceeding the 4294967296-byte limit by 58662912 bytes. Guard cleanup was confirmed.
driverObservation: The driver reported 57721368 heap-used bytes at export and 520514344 at download despite avoiding eager assertion-message formatting. This single sample does not identify retained objects or prove the cause of the peak.
cleanup: The temporary project was independently hash-verified and deleted; the worktree, verified dependency junction and individually verified temporary package files were removed. Only small evidence artifacts were retained.
limitations: The prototype lacks production security, compatibility, cancellation and lifecycle validation and is not integrated. The run does not solve the large-project resource, numeric ownership, native, hosted-CI or M2 completion gates.
